gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the brightness gap between the Chigee and Carpuride screens is only a peak figure. Chigee's own AIO-5 comparison table rates both the AIO-5 Play and AIO-5 Lite at 1000 nits, with 1200 nits as a separate peak row. Carpuride gives a flat 1000 nits for the W502/W702/W619. On a like-for-like basis the $399.99 Play is no brighter than the $269.99 Carpuride, and the $105 Aoocci C3 is 800 nits.
standout_why: I compared against throttlebuff.com/best-motorcycle-carplay-screens (opened 2026-11-14) and motorcyclegpshub.com/best-motorcycle-carplay-android-auto (opened 2026-11-14). Throttlebuff gives the AIO-5 EVO 'up to 1,200 nits' next to Carpuride's 'up to 1,000 nits', which makes Chigee look 20% brighter, and never gives Chigee's 1000-nit figure. Motorcyclegpshub gives no nits, IP ratings or prices and only calls the AIO-5 Lite 'bright, waterproof'. Neither page covers a battery-powered unit, and neither gives the Aoocci C3's 800 nits or the AIO-5 Lite's IP67 against the Play's IP68. Throttlebuff does state the 5 V / 2.5 A USB minimum for Carpuride, so that power point is partly covered already. I could not open the handlebarhq.com list (TLS certificate error), so I did not compare against it.
decides: This takes brightness out as a reason to pay more. In ChatGPT's line-up the AIO-5 Play ($399.99) and the Carpuride W702/W502 ($269.99) are both 1000 nits, so the $130 difference buys IP68 against IP67, the brand and its features. It does not buy a brighter screen. The 'budget' Aoocci C3 really is dimmer at 800 nits. For a 'portable' buyer the deciding spec is the power source. The Carpuride needs 12 V at 1 A from the battery, or a USB port that holds above 4.5 V at 2.5 A. The AIO-5 Lite is hardwired (battery plus ACC wire). Only the Aoocci F5 claims to run without bike power, and I could not source its battery capacity or runtime. So the F5 stays the portable pick on Aoocci's word alone, and its price has fallen to $189 from the $199 ChatGPT showed.
